correctness.rationale: The central triangle puts the origin strictly in the interior. The lower parabolic chords have increasing slopes, with the central slopes −2 and 2 between the left and right parabolic chains. Normalizing each supporting inequality to right side one gives the reciprocal-pair polar vertices, the two central vertices and the upper vertex as stated. In reciprocal variables inserting w into u>w>v clips exactly one triangle on either side, with each determinant (u−v)(u−w)(w−v); the removed total area equals the decrease in one third of the cubic-gap sum. The two-knot shoelace base is 3−s+s²+s³. Thus the polar cubic-gap formula holds; complementary divisors convert its gaps to the original gaps divided by h. Primal trapezoids give (4h³+2−S_h)/3, establishing reciprocity including the finite h term. For limit calculations add 0 to the reciprocal mesh, obtaining P_h=8/3+F(X_h)/3+h^−3. The full and odd mesh sums follow by telescoping the partial fractions; in the odd sum with x=1,3,… the summand is (3/2)(1/x−1/(x+2))−(3/2)(1/x²+1/(x+2)²)+(1/x³−1/(x+2)³), giving 4−3π²/8. Adding knots only decreases F. Even heights contain 1/2, giving F≤1/4; odd heights are subsets of the odd mesh, giving F≥4−3π²/8. The proposed prime and 2p sequences converge to their finite meshes. Both LCM sequences exhaust their respective meshes in the limit: once a prefix is included the possible tail discrepancy is at most the cube of the last prefix knot. This proves all sharp endpoints, not a claim of the largest gap. Own supplemental exact hull/intersection checks reproduced the areas and reciprocity for h=2,…,80 (/workspace/branches/independent_replay.py, polygons()). The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The polar area of a natural arithmetic building block for reflexive polytope constructions is a meaningful geometric invariant. The calculation exhibits exact cancellation of cubic-gap contributions across primal and dual areas and makes the entire known normalized primal spectrum transferable to the polar. This is more than lower-dimensional numeric evidence or a restatement of the primal area theorem.
